facts.statement: The animal is known from a single nearly complete skeleton found in the Tiaojishan Formation.
facts.quote: Qinglongopterus is known from only one specimen; D3080/3081, a nearly complete skeleton collected from the Tiaojishan Formation.

facts.statement: Lü Junchang and colleagues described the genus in 2012.
facts.quote: It was described by Lü Junchang et al. in 2012.

facts.statement: It lived during the Middle to Upper Jurassic in Mutoudeng, Qinglong County, Hebei Province, China.
facts.quote: Qinglongopterus is a genus of rhamphorhynchid pterosaur from the Middle/Upper Jurassic of Mutoudeng, Qinglong County, Hebei Province, China.

facts.statement: It is classified as a rhamphorhynchid pterosaur.
facts.quote: Qinglongopterus is a genus of rhamphorhynchid pterosaur

facts.statement: Large eye sockets and a lack of skeletal fusion suggest the holotype was a late-stage juvenile.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen has large eye sockets and exhibits a relative lack of fusion throughout the skeleton, suggesting the individual was a late-stage juvenile.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen had an estimated wingspan of 34.4 centimeters.
facts.quote: The holotype has an estimated wingspan of 34.4 centimeters (13.5 inches).

facts.statement: Researchers suggest Rhamphorhynchus may have descended from Qinglongopterus due to many shared traits.
facts.quote: In the original description, the authors suggest Rhamphorhynchus may even be descended from Qinglongopterus due to the large number of shared characters between the two genera.

facts.statement: The similarity between the two genera may indicate evolutionary stasis within rhamphorhynchine pterosaurs.
facts.quote: This may be evidence of evolutionary stasis within rhamphorhynchine pterosaurs.

facts.statement: It lived between 168.2 and 152.21 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Bathonian to Kimmeridgian (168.2 to 152.21 million years ago)

rejected.statement: The animal resembles Rhamphorhynchus but has a proportionally smaller head and shorter wings.
rejected.quote: Qinglongopterus is noted to be remarkably similar to Rhamphorhynchus, although Qinglongopterus has a proportionally smaller head and shorter wings.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'has a proportionally smaller head and shorter wings'
